• Home: pick the featured card (it changes every 2 minutes) or any game in the rows below.
• Diamonds: check in daily for +1 diamond. Each game gives 1 free play per day (monthly plan: 3, yearly plan: unlimited); after that each game costs 1 diamond. A win earns +1 diamond.
• Playing with friends: each game costs every player 1 diamond (free plays do not apply), and the winner gets +1 diamond. Monthly and yearly plans pay no diamonds.
• Win streaks: 3 wins in a row in one game give +2 diamonds, 5 in a row give +3.
• Loyalty bonus: after a 30-day check-in streak, each next check-in gives +2 diamonds (monthly plan: +4).
• Modes: play the computer (you move first), a friend nearby, or online by exchanging a room code or QR. Some games also support 3-4 players against the computer.
• Computer levels: 7 levels from Easy to Supreme. Only Easy is open at first; beating a level unlocks the next one for that game. The yearly plan unlocks every level and removes diamonds entirely.
• Time per move (all games): 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 or 30 minutes, or 1 hour. Against the computer it follows the level (Easy 1 min ... Supreme 1 h); against people the host picks one of these seven. If time runs out, the player to move loses.
• Shop: remove ads, get more free plays or buy diamonds.
• Change language and nickname in Settings.

Goal: as in Gomoku, get 5 of your own stones in a row (horizontal, vertical or diagonal); a line blocked at both ends does not count.
• The twist: both players share one set of stones in 4 colours (blue, red, purple, yellow). The board shows only colours, never whose stone is whose.
• The first player (X) picks any colour on the palette at the bottom each turn, then taps the board.
• The second player (O) must answer with a stone of the same colour the first player just placed.
• You must remember where your stones (and your opponent's) are. X and O marks appear only when the game ends.
• Tip: the first player can keep switching colours to confuse; as the second player, remember positions, not colours.

Goal: make five or more of your marks in a row, across, down or diagonally. X (dark) moves first.
• The board is endless: drag with one finger to move around, pinch to zoom.
• If both ends of your line are blocked by enemy marks, it does not count.
• Tap an empty cell to place your mark. Block your opponent's open threes and fours!

Goal: checkmate the enemy king.
• Pawns step forward and capture diagonally. Knights jump in an L. Bishops slide diagonally, rooks slide straight, queens do both, kings step one square.
• Special moves: castling, en passant and promotion on the last rank.
• Tap a piece, then a highlighted square. A game is drawn by stalemate, the 50-move rule or too few pieces.
• Repetition: a move that recreates an earlier position loses for the player who made it.

Goal: control more of the board than your opponent. Black moves first.
• Capture: a group of stones with no empty point next to it (no liberties) is removed from the board.
• Forbidden: you may not play a move that leaves your own group with no liberties (unless it captures), and you may not repeat an earlier board position.
• Ending: when your opponent passes and nothing useful is left, tap End game to score the position.
• Scoring: by area - your stones plus the empty regions only you border. White receives 7.5 komi. Dead stones are not removed automatically, so capture them before you pass.
• Tap an intersection to preview a stone, then press Place stone.

• Easy: for newcomers. The computer looks only one or two moves ahead and often plays at random; knowing the rules is enough to win.
• Medium: avoids obvious blunders but still makes many mistakes. Play with a plan.
• Good: knows basic tactics. Calculate a few moves ahead and leave no weaknesses.
• Strong: rarely errs and plans ahead. You need a clear strategy to win.
• Master: solid, very few mistakes. Only experienced players win regularly.
• Challenger: almost never makes a tactical mistake. Beating it is something to be proud of.
• Supreme: the computer at full strength. In chess it plays like a 2800 Elo engine (CCRL engine rating scale): nearly unbeatable for humans.
• Each level is clearly stronger than the one below: the higher level wins most games (about 65% to 98%).
• Challenge your mind: how far can you climb? Start at Easy, conquer each level and reach Supreme.

Goal: fill the 7×7 board with the numbers 1 to 49, each exactly once, so that every row, every column and both main diagonals add up to 175.
• Puzzle: one puzzle per day, starting with one given number in one cell. It always has a solution, and any arrangement that follows the rules wins.
• Placing: tap a cell, then tap a number. Picking a number already on the board moves it to the selected cell.
• Sums: the right column shows each row's sum, the bottom row each column's sum, and the top bar both diagonals. Green: 7 cells filled and exactly 175. Red: over 175, or full but wrong.
• Hints: 10 per day with the monthly plan, 20 per day with the yearly plan. Hinted cells are locked.
• Leaving midway costs nothing: come back the same day to continue. Once solved, the next puzzle arrives tomorrow.
• Tip: 175 = 7 × 25, so 25 sits halfway between 1 and 49. Try placing pairs that add up to 50 (1 + 49, 2 + 48...) symmetrically around the center.

Goal: be the first to reach the opposite side of the board.
• Move: step one square up, down, left or right. If an opponent's pawn is next to you, jump over it, or step diagonally if a wall or the edge is behind it.
• Walls: instead of moving you may place a wall two squares long. Walls cannot overlap or cross, and you may never block every path to a goal.
• Walls left: 10 each with 2 players, 5 each with 4 players.
• Build: choose Wall, tap near the crossing where it goes to preview it (green = allowed), then press Place wall.
• Repetition: in 2-player games, a pawn move that recreates an earlier position loses; in 4-player games such a move is not allowed.

Goal: fill every empty square so each row, column and 3×3 box contains the digits 1 to 9 once.
• Entering: tap a square, then a number. Wrong numbers show in red; fix them with Erase.
• Notes: switch on the pencil to jot small candidate numbers (shown in red) in a square.
• Erase clears the selected square. Each 3×3 box starts with only one given number (9 in total), so any grid that follows the rules wins.

Goal: use all 7 pieces (2 large triangles, 1 medium triangle, 2 small triangles, 1 square, 1 parallelogram) to fill the grey shape exactly, with no overlaps and no pieces left over.
• Each round has 10 random shapes, from compact to spiky. You have 3 minutes per shape.
• If time runs out on any shape you lose; finish all 10 to win.
• Drag pieces from the tray onto the shape. Tap to rotate 45°, long-press the parallelogram to flip it.
• Drop a piece near a corner of the shape or of another piece and it snaps into place.
• Any arrangement that fills the shape exactly counts.
• Tip: place the two large triangles first; they cover half the area.
• 7 levels by number of pieces: Easy 4, Medium 5, Good 6, Strong 7 (the classic set), Master 8, Challenger 9, Supreme 10. Finish all 10 shapes of a level to unlock the next.

Goal: end the game with more territory than your rivals.
• Setup: take turns placing your stones on empty squares (4 each with 2 players, 3 with 3 players, 2 with 4 players).
• Your turn: choose one of your stones and move it 0, 1 or 2 squares up, down, left or right. It cannot pass through walls or other stones.
• Wall: after moving you MUST place a wall on one free side of the square you stand on.
• Territory: when every walled-off area holds stones of only one player, the game ends. You score the squares of the areas that contain only your stones.
• Ties: the larger single area wins; otherwise it is a draw. A player who cannot move skips the turn.

Goal: within 10 minutes, build 7 English words on the given theme (for example Cities: PARIS, VIENNA, ...) from wooden letter blocks.
• The blocks are exactly the letters of the 7 answer words, shuffled. Each block can be used once.
• Every puzzle has exactly one solution: only one set of 7 theme words uses up all the blocks. Only those 7 words are accepted; a word on the theme that is not an answer is rejected.
•
• Tap a block to add its letter to the current word, tap it again to remove it. Delete removes the last letter, Clear removes the whole word. Press Submit to enter the word.
• Build all 7 words to win; when the 10 minutes run out you lose and the answer words are shown.
• Tap the ? button during play to see how to play again.
• Tip: look for rare letters such as Q, Z, J, X and V first; they usually belong to only one word.
• Plan perks: the monthly plan shows each word's length in the answer boxes; the yearly plan adds 2 hints per round, each placing one word for you.

Goal: checkmate the enemy general. Red moves first.
• The general and advisors stay inside the palace. The two generals may never face each other on an open file.
• Elephants move two points diagonally, cannot cross the river and can be blocked at the midpoint.
• Horses move like an L but are blocked by an adjacent piece. Chariots slide straight.
• Cannons slide straight and capture by jumping over exactly one piece. Soldiers step forward, and sideways after crossing the river.
• A player with no legal move loses. In this app, a move that recreates an earlier position loses for the player who made it.
